IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD  R/FIRST APPEAL NO. 1822 of 2015  ==========================================================

 MR MEHUL S SHAH(772) for the Appellant(s) No. 1,2  MR C S SHUKLA(7549) for the Defendant(s) No. 1  MR RATHIN P RAVAL(5013) for the Defendant(s) No. 4  RULE SERVED for the Defendant(s) No. 2,3  ================

sentences.text: ORAL ORDER 1.

The present First Appeal, under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, is preferred by the appellant/s - original claimant/s - legal heirs of the deceased - Rushirajsinh Vaghela, being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the judgment and award dated 13.02.2015 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Aux.), Bhavnagar in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.751 of 2008, by which the Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.3,64,500/- with 9% per annum interest to the claimant/s, holding Opponents liable, jointly and severally.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claim Petition No.751 of 2008
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text:
2. Brief facts of the case are as under:
2.1 That on 30.-09.2008, deceased Rushirajsinh Kiritsinh Vaghela was travelling in ST Bus No.GJ-18V-9950 from Bhavnagar to Gadhada after completing work of diamond NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1822/2015 ORDER DATED: 11/10/2024 Kiritsinh Mansinh Vaghela vs Gujarat State Road Transport ... on 11 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38844505/

sentences.text: undefined polishing at Bhavnagar, ST driver was driving his bus with full speed and when said bus reached near Gadhula village, at that time opponent no.1 came with Truck No.GTK-2695 with full speed and rash and negligent manner and dashed with ST Bus and on account of said accident, serious injuries were caused to the deceased and died during treatment.

Therefore, the parents of the deceased have filed claim petition seeking compensation of Rs.8,00,000/- with cost and interest for unnatural and untimely death against the present respondents before the Tribunal.
2.2 Notices were served to the opponents.

Opponents - Gujarat State Road Transport Corporation and Insurance Company have appeared and has filed its written statement / objections by disputing all the averments made by the claimant in the claim petition.
2.3 The Tribunal has framed the issues.
The oral as well as documentary evidence were led by the rival parties before the Tribunal.
After considering the documentary as well as oral evidence and submissions made at the bar, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition by awarding compensation as noted above.

2.4 Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal,
the present appeal is preferred by the claimant/s for enhancement.

3. Learned advocate for the appellant/s - claimant/s has submitted that the Tribunal has committed an error in not NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1822/2015 ORDER DATED: 11/10/2024 undefined properly calculating the amount of compensation.

He has submitted that amount of award is on lower side as the Tribunal has not properly considered the various aspects; like prospective income of the deceased, negligence, liability and family circumstances, etc.
He has submitted that the deceased was aged about only 22 years at the time of accident and was doing diamond polishing and was unmarried.
He has submitted that at the relevant point of time, his monthly income was Rs.5000/- per month.

He has submitted that therefore, considering the loss of dependency, it would be calculated as Rs.3333/- x 12 months, the amount would be Rs.40,000/- per year, and as per II schedule, the amount would be Rs.7,20,000/- and Rs.2,40,000/- to be deducted towards personal expenses.
Total Rs.4,80,000/- should be awarded to the claimants by the learned Tribunal.
He has further submitted that considering the general and non-pecuniary damages, the learned Tribunal should award Rs.2,000/- towards loss of estate and Rs.2,500/- towards funeral expenses.
He has submitted that the compensation is required to be enhanced by modifying the award impugned accordingly and this appeal may be allowed.
4. Per contra, learned advocate for respondent - Insurance Company has submitted that the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is just and proper.
The Tribunal has rightly considered the income of the deceased, the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1822/2015 ORDER DATED: 11/10/2024 undefined age of the deceased, the dependency and future aspect of income.

sentences.text: He has submitted that under the head of loss of estate and funeral expenses, the Tribunal has rightly awarded compensation.
He has submitted that the amount under the head of loss of consortium is just and proper.

He has submitted that this appeal may be dismissed and no interference be made by this Court.
5.
It is noteworthy to mention that the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 which gives paramount importance to the concept of 'just and fair' compensation.
It is a beneficial legislation which has been framed with the object of providing relief to the victims or their families.
Section 168 of the Motor Vehicles Act deals with the concept of 'just compensation' which ought to be determined on the foundation of fairness, reasonableness and equitability.

Although such determination can never be arithmetically exact or perfect, an endeavor should be made by the Court to award just and fair compensation irrespective of the amount claimed by the claimants.
6.1 I have considered the submissions made by the rival parties.
I have perused the record and proceedings of the Tribunal.
I have gone through the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.
From the record, it transpires that the deceased was aged about 22 years and was doing work of diamond polishing and his monthly income was Rs.3333/- at the relevant point of time.
Therefore, it should be considered as monthly income of the deceased.
Hence, it would come to Rs.40,000/- per year.
As per II schedule, the amount would NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1822/2015 ORDER DATED: 11/10/2024 undefined come to Rs.7,20,000/-.

Since the deceased is aged about 22 years, 1/3rd would be proper to be deducted as personal expenses and therefore, it total amount would come to Rs.4,80,000/- (Rs.7,20,000/- minus Rs.2,40,000/-) and same is required to be awarded to the claimants.

6.2 Further, considering the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Pranay Shethi (supra), as general and non-pecuniary damages, under the head of loss of estate and funeral expenses, if we award Rs.2000/- and Rs.2500/-, respectively, which would be the just and proper compensation.

6.3 Therefore, total compensation would be as under, which the claimant/s is/are entitled to get.
 Particulars Am  Future Loss of Income   Loss of Estate   Funeral Expenses   Total...
Less : Amount which is already awarded   Additional amount which is awarded

7. Therefore, I hold that the claimant/s are entitled to get the total amount of compensation of Rs.4,84,500/- with 9% p.a. interest from the date of filing the claim petition till its realisation, which would meet the ends of justice.
Rest of the direction(s) of the Tribunal remain same.

The Tribunal has NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1822/2015 ORDER DATED: 11/10/2024 undefined already awarded Rs.3,64,500/-, therefore, remaining amount of Rs.1,20,000/- would be the enhanced Kiritsinh Mansinh Vaghela vs Gujarat State Road Transport ... on 11 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38844505/
3 amount of compensation payable to the claimant/s.

sentences.text: 8. For the reasons recorded above, the following order is passed.
8.1 The present appeal is partly allowed.

8.2 The respondents are directed to deposit the enhanced amount Rs.1,20,000/- with 7.5% p.a.
interest from the date of claim petition till its realisation before the concerned Tribunal, within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of this order.

8.3 The Tribunal shall disburse the entire awarded amount lying in the FDR and/or with the Tribunal, with accrued interest thereon, if any, to the claimants, by account payee cheque / NEFT /
RTGS, after proper verification and after following due procedure.

8.4 While making the payment, the Tribunal shall deduct the courts fees, if not paid, in accordance with rules/law.
8.5
Record and proceedings be sent back to the concerned Tribunal, forthwith.
